'''Pentecaust notifications''' tell a MELEK user that somebody has messaged them in [[Pentecaust]], without requiring them to go and look. A letter icon in the MELEK navigation bar carries an unread count; clicking it opens a notifications page, and clicking an item opens that conversation in the Pentecaust messenger.

== Why it was needed ==

Pentecaust messaging worked, but nothing told anyone a message had arrived. A messenger that only works if you remember to check it is a messenger most people stop checking. The notification is the piece that makes the rest of it usable.

== How unread is determined ==

The notification system does not keep its own copy of anyone's messages. It derives everything from the existing chat store, and stores exactly one thing of its own: a '''per-account read marker''' recording how far that account has read in each conversation. Anything after the marker is unread.

This matters for two reasons. It means there is no second database of private messages to secure or to drift out of sync, and it means marking something read is a tiny write rather than a mutation of message history.

Both kinds of conversation are covered — direct messages and team channels — and each notification carries the kind of conversation it came from and the link that opens it.

== Security ==

Adding a notification does not widen the attack surface in the way one might expect, because the notification carries no message content of its own and grants no new access: it is a pointer into a conversation the account could already open.

The one real risk in a feature like this is '''navigation''': a notification is attacker-influenced content, since anyone can send a message, and a link rendered from it could point anywhere. The rendering is therefore locked down so that nothing inserted by a sender can navigate a user off-site. Text that looks like a URL is rendered as inert text rather than as a working link unless it points somewhere the system itself serves.

A related protection on the messaging side is a word filter that masks a list of exact-spelled profanities. It is deliberately narrow: it matches whole words with exact spelling and '''does not''' chase misspellings. That is a requirement rather than an oversight — a filter aggressive enough to catch every variant also mangles ordinary writing, and the goal here is to keep casual profanity out of a default view, not to build censorship that cannot be worked around.

== The icon ==

The MELEK navigation icon is a plain grey outline of a letter, drawn to match the existing pencil and magnifying-glass icons rather than a filled, coloured, cartoon envelope. It sits beside them and carries a numeric badge with the unread count.

== Status ==

Built and tested. At the time of writing the change is still in an unmerged pull request, so the notifications page is not yet live and the link returns a 404 until that is merged.
